basis: Cowden cutaneous and oral hamartomas define disease; thyroid nodules in 1/2 support gland occupation. Associated carcinomas are separate predisposition outcomes.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: benign thyroid nodular lesions are part of Cowden disease and reported in 1/2; gland occupation qualifies independently of cancer risk.

basis: Developmental, dental and gonadal abnormalities define syndrome; radioulnar defects occur in 80-99%. Acne omitted at cap; unspecified renal morphology does not establish damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: abnormal teeth and deficient enamel explicitly characterize the syndrome; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Short-rib skeletal dysplasia with polydactyly; thoracic restriction alone does not establish direct lung damage. Subtype-specific pulmonary hypoplasia frequency is unavailable.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pulmonary hypoplasia affecting at least 30% is not established for this subtype; skeletal thoracic restriction alone is insufficient.

basis: A cavernous vascular lesion directly involves retinal blood vessels, establishing both retinal and vascular disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the lesion intrinsically affects retinal vascular channels; the cardiovascular axis includes local blood vessels and does not require systemic disease.

basis: Multiple ischemic cerebral infarctions define the dementia; brain injury and cerebrovascular occlusive disease are intrinsic to the concept.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: repeated cerebral infarctions define a cerebrovascular disease; cerebral vessels fall within the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Progressive cerebral astrogliopathy defines disease. Scoliosis occurs in 30-79% but is secondary to neurologic impairment rather than direct skeletal pathology.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis is frequent (30-79%) but reflects secondary neuromuscular deformity; direct skeletal disease is not established.

basis: Neurodegeneration defines disease; muscle atrophy (30-79%) is neurogenic rather than direct myopathy. Ophthalmoplegia reflects neural motor dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 30-79%, but results from motor neuron/peripheral nerve degeneration rather than direct muscle disease.

basis: The membrane-stabilizing toxidrome directly impairs cardiac conduction and contractility and CNS function, with characteristic seizures or coma.

decisions.neurologic: primary: direct CNS toxicity, including seizures or coma, is a characteristic component of the membrane-stabilizing poisoning syndrome.

basis: Precursor T-cell malignancy affects marrow and blood; supplied synonyms and ancestry include the lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma entity.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: the supplied concept encompasses precursor T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma; lymphoma explicitly requires this mechanism axis.

basis: A brainstem medial longitudinal fasciculus lesion causes impaired coordinated eye movements; intrinsic ocular disease is not required.

decisions.ocular: none: the lesion is in the brainstem ocular motor pathway; abnormal eye movement does not establish direct disease of the eye.
